research_page.title: Robotic Optical Inspection & Metrology
research_page.lead: As part of an IGF-funded research project (01IF22263N) at Technologie Campus Teisnach Optik (TH Deggendorf), I contributed to an automated cobotic inspection system designed to detect microscopic imperfections on precision optical surfaces.
research_page.paper_title: Cobotic Inspection of Surface Imperfections with Collimated Illumination
research_page.paper_doi_label: Access Official SPIE Paper via DOI (10.1117/12.3111698)
research_page.thesis_title: Robotic Inspection of Imperfections on Optical Surfaces
research_page.thesis_status: Release pending institutional review & partner clearance
research_page.thesis_note: In accordance with institutional guidelines, the PDF will be made downloadable once formal release permissions are finalized.

sections.challenge_text: High-precision optical components require rigorous quality control to detect minute surface defects (scratches, digs, dust, sub-surface damage) that impair laser transmission or optical imaging. Manual microscopic inspection is slow, operator-fatiguing, and subjective, while conventional Cartesian multi-axis stages lack the kinematic flexibility required for inspecting curved, freeform optical geometries at controlled angles.
sections.robotics_text: The inspection platform centers on a 6-axis collaborative robot (FANUC CR-7iA/L). By mounting the optical sensor head on the robot flange, the system can follow precise surface-normal trajectories across complex optical elements while maintaining strict focal distance and illumination angles.
sections.optics_text: A specialized collimated directional illumination array combined with high-resolution digital imaging provides sharp defect contrast. The experimental setup demonstrated repeatable defect-detection capability down to approximately 6 µm on calibrated reference targets.
sections.cad_text: Using PTC Creo Parametric and Dassault SolidWorks, I designed custom test-rig adapter plates, camera/illumination mounting brackets, calibration targets, and protective safety structures to ensure mechanical stiffness and eliminate micro-vibrations during image capture.
sections.results_text: The robotic inspection station reliably detected surface imperfections down to ~6 µm on test specimens. The findings co-authored by Kunal were published in the SPIE Proceedings (2026) under the title 'Cobotic Inspection of Surface Imperfections with Collimated Illumination' (DOI: 10.1117/12.3111698).

about_page.title: About Kunal Bhai Patel
about_page.lead: Mechanical & Mechatronics Engineer, Builder, and Technology Enthusiast based in Germany. Grounded in rigorous CAD design, robotic automation, and physical maker experimentation.
about_page.intro_title: Engineering by Profession. Maker by Curiosity.
about_page.intro_text: My background brings together mechanical engineering and mechatronics. During my research work at Technologie Campus Teisnach Optik, I helped develop a robotic setup for inspecting microscopic imperfections on optical surfaces. Outside the lab, I am happiest solving practical problems at my workbench — whether that means refining a 3D-printed mechanism, getting a pen plotter to draw reliably over Wi-Fi, or configuring an older computer as a private Debian home server.

about_page.training_text: Currently expanding advanced engineering CAD capabilities through intensive Creo Konstrukteur professional qualification: parametric modeling, complex assemblies, skeleton/top-down modeling, surfacing, sheet metal, and GD&T technical drawings.
about_page.workshop_text: To me, engineering is fundamentally about turning concepts into physical reality. My workshop is where theory meets practical tolerances: tuning FDM printers for functional mechanical parts with heat-set brass inserts, programming ESP32 microcontrollers with FluidNC, and building quiet thermal enclosures for data storage. Not everything works on the first attempt — iterative troubleshooting is where real engineering mastery is developed.

website_section.title: About This Website
website_section.text: This portfolio website is itself an independent engineering project. Rather than using generic templates or heavy commercial frameworks, it was designed and built as a clean, deterministic static-site architecture using standard HTML5, modern CSS with CSS custom properties, vanilla JavaScript, and a lightweight Python 3 build engine. It features native bilingual routing (EN/DE), instant switchable Light and Dark themes with zero flash, deep-link persistence, and free static hosting on GitHub Pages. AI-assisted development tools were purposefully directed to streamline build scripting, template compilation, and structured content management — demonstrating disciplined technical direction and practical problem-solving.
